summary: Republican incumbent Pete Ricketts ran for reelection and won, defeating independent Dan Osborn.

candidates.name: Pete Ricketts
candidates.bio: Pete Ricketts is the Republican U.S. Senator from Nebraska and a former governor of the state. He cosponsored the National Right-to-Work Act.

positions.summary: Says he opposes out-of-control federal spending and the national debt, and supports spending limits, less regulation and a more orderly appropriations process.
Calls border security essential to national security and supports asylum reform, building the border wall, higher federal penalties for fentanyl distributors and stopping sanctuary cities.
Says he wants the federal government out of the classroom, favors local education with parental control, and supports school choice.
Says he backs domestic energy production, biofuels, faster permitting and nuclear power, and opposes federal rules and electric-vehicle mandates he sees as overreach.
Describes himself as pro-life, signed a ban on dismemberment abortion as governor, and supports barring federal taxpayer funding of abortions.

candidates.name: Dan Osborn
candidates.bio: Dan Osborn is an independent and former Omaha labor leader. He ran for Senate for a second time after his 2024 campaign.

positions.summary: Says he will cut waste, end corporate welfare, and refuse to vote for spending the country cannot afford.
Says no one should go bankrupt from medical debt, supports the Break Up Big Medicine Act, and pledges never to vote to cut Medicare or Social Security benefits.
Calls for meaningful immigration reform with vetting and more immigration judges and lawyers, and supports the 1,500 additional border agents in a border bill.
Says the country should have a Roe standard, and his campaign said he supports codifying the Roe standard.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35); also confirmed by wowt.com report. Shares refreshed Nov. 25, 2026 from the Nebraska Secretary of State page, still labeled Unofficial Results. State canvass is set for Nov. 30.
